title: Parallax - Embeddings & Rerank Discovery
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
summary: Discovery call to understand Parallax's retrieval + rerank use case, existing vector DB footprint, target throughput and latency, and security constraints. Parallax is evaluating Redwood Hosted for quick onboarding but is curious about Dedicated for production latency and Private for data residency. Key asks: integration patterns with existing vector DB (Pinecone/Milvus), expected QPS and latency for 1M-5M vectors, embedding dimensionality tradeoffs, and feasibility of running cross-encoder rerank on Redwood Dedicated. Next steps include sharing pricing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, a benchmark runbook, and scheduling a 1-week pilot with sample data.
action_items: Jordan Kim: Send Hosted/Dedicated/Private pricing sheet + SSO/SAML and SOC2 summary by 2026-03-06
Samira Patel: Share benchmark runbook, sample docker config and recommended embedding batch sizes by 2026-03-08
Evan Torres: Provide sample query logs and expected QPS profile (p95 latency targets) by 2026-03-10
Marcus Lee: Confirm network constraints for Private (VPC peering possibility) by 2026-03-09
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and security docs
Customer to share sample dataset and query distribution
Follow-up demo to show Dedicated performance and rerank pipeline
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the inference team, and with me is Samira, our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:12] Evan (Parallax CTO): Evan here, CTO at Parallax. Priya, Marcus and Alex are on as well. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:20] Samira (Redwood SE): Awesome. High level, I want to understand your retrieval stack today, how you're doing candidate generation and reranking, and what your SLA/throughput needs look like.
[00:35] Priya (Lead ML): Sure. Quick context: we run a search product for developer docs and internal knowledge. Currently we use Pinecone for vector storage and a lightweight BM25 layer for keyword fallback. Candidate generation is a 256-d bi-encoder embeddings call; then we do a cross-encoder rerank in-house for top 50 candidates. The reranker is expensive; that's why we're evaluating options to move parts of the pipeline to a vendor.
[01:05] Jordan: Great. What's your current QPS and target latency for end-to-end search?
[01:12] Marcus (Infra): Right now peak is around 120 QPS, sustained 30-50 QPS. E2E p95 is ~420ms, mostly dominated by the cross-encoder rerank which runs on CPU instances. Target p95 is sub-200ms ideally.
[01:30] Samira: Okay that helps. A couple routes here: Hosted Redwood can handle the embedding generation and we can route candidates to your vector DB (Pinecone) and return to you for rerank. For the rerank, we usually recommend Dedicated if you're doing cross-encoder rerank at scale since it avoids network hops and can run on GPU with much lower latency.
[01:55] Evan: When you say Dedicated, is that reserved GPU pools? And what's the orchestration/ops burden?
[02:05] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput. We manage runtime, autoscaling policies, and you get SLA-backed latency. Ops burden for you is minimal — we provide configs and a control plane. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you host the control plane and we provide an appliance for inference. That adds more infra responsibility on your side but meets stricter compliance.
[02:35] Priya: For the reranker specifically, we were thinking cross-encoder like large re-rankers (eg. 3B). Do you support mixed precision and quantized weights?
[02:45] Samira: Yes, the runtime supports quantization-friendly execution paths and we have kernel selection optimizations. For cross-encoders, we typically recommend Dedicated with a quantized 4-bit profile for cost-efficiency if accuracy hit is acceptable.
[02:58] Alex (Product): What about embedding dimensionality tradeoffs? We're experimenting with 768 and 1024 dims. Storage and recall changes matter to our product.
[03:08] Samira: Right — higher dimensionality gives more representational power but increases vector DB storage and nearest neighbor latency. For Milvus/Pinecone-style indexes, HNSW performance scales with vector dim but it's mostly dependent on index params and ef/construction. If you can get similar quality at 768 it's cheaper. We usually recommend benchmarking both with your query set.
[03:35] Evan: On integration, we do host our Pinecone instance; can Redwood hook into an external vector DB or do you expect customers to migrate?
[03:45] Jordan: We support both patterns. For quick pilots, we integrate with Pinecone/Milvus/Weaviate — calls: Redwood will output embeddings via API or webhook; you can push to your existing DB. For tight latency and rerank co-location, some customers move vectors into Redwood Dedicated's local index or use our integrated cache for hot vectors.
[04:10] Marcus: If we keep Pinecone, what's the typical round-trip for embedding->search->rerank vs moving everything to Dedicated?
[04:20] Samira: If embedding service is hosted and you call Pinecone over the network, expect additional 30-70ms depending on region and throughput. Cross-encoder rerank on Dedicated on-GPU reduces rerank latency from hundreds ms to tens of ms. End-to-end numbers: hosted embedding + remote Pinecone + external rerank ~ 350-600ms p95 depending on model; Dedicated with co-located vector storage and on-GPU rerank can push that under 200ms p95 for many workloads.
[04:55] Priya: That's promising. Our main constraint: data residency and PII. We need SOC2 and KMS support, and any embeddings with PII must not leave our VPC in some scenarios.
[05:08] Jordan: Got it. We have SOC2, and Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem where control plane sits in your environment. We also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and in transit. We'll include the security pack in the email.
[05:25] Evan: Regarding throughput — if we move to Dedicated, what QPS per GPU are we looking at for a bi-encoder embed + HNSW ANN at 1M vectors?
[05:36] Samira: It depends on embedding size and batcher. For 768-d embeddings on A100-like hardware, embedding throughput might be 800-1200 embeds/s per GPU when batched efficiently. For ANN search on 1M vectors with HNSW — approximate query latency is sub 5-20ms per query depending on ef search settings; throughput can be hundreds to low thousands QPS if index fits in memory. If you're running a cross-encoder rerank on GPU for top-50, that'll be the heavier work — like 100-300 qps on a single GPU depending on model size and quantization.
[06:15] Marcus: So to hit 200 QPS end-to-end with cross-encoder rerank we'll need multiple GPUs?
[06:22] Samira: Likely. You can also shard the rerank across multiples or use a bi-encoder-only flow with a lighter cross-encoder for quality-sensitive cases. We can size a Dedicated pool — e.g., 4 GPUs for steady 200 QPS with p95 targets — we'll provide modeled numbers in the sizing sheet.
[06:40] Priya: How do you handle hybrid search — like keyword filtering + vector? We rely on filters (product meta) heavily.
[06:48] Samira: We support hybrid pipelines: you can do a filtered ANN query (vector search with metadata filters) if your vector DB supports it (Pinecone does). Another pattern is to run a boolean/keyword first-pass to narrow candidate set and then embed+ANN within those. For rerank, the cross-encoder can ingest the original text + metadata features. We can show examples in the runbook.
[07:15] Evan: Any concerns about vector dimensionality and CPU costs when storing at 1024 dims for 5M vectors?
[07:22] Samira: Storage costs scale linearly; 1024 dims is ~33% larger than 768 dims. For 5M vectors, you'd want to estimate storage plus index overhead. Also for disk-backed indexes, disk IO can become the bottleneck; we recommend in-memory for top-tier latency. We can include a cost estimate.
[07:42] Alex: What about incremental updates and TTLs? We have frequent small updates — a few thousand vectors per day.
[07:49] Jordan: That's fine; most vector DBs handle dynamic insert/delete. On Dedicated, you can configure background index maintenance and hot caches. If you're doing heavy churn, we recommend smaller index segments and periodic rebuilds. We'll share configuration tips.
[08:05] Marcus: On networking for Private — is peering required? Latency concerns if control plane is separate.
[08:12] Samira: For Private deployments we typically do VPC peering or private link. If you want fully air-gapped, we have an on-prem package but that increases ops. We'll capture the networking options in the security docs.
[08:28] Evan: A couple of quick technical clarifications: 1) What embedding model sizes do you support in Hosted? 2) Can we run custom models on Dedicated/Private?
[08:36] Samira: Hosted exposes a curated model catalog (open models we host), including 384/768/1024-d embeddings depending on model. Dedicated and Private allow you to bring-your-own-models (BYOM) — customers often bring a fine-tuned bi-encoder or a family of models. For cross-encoder rerank, Dedicated supports larger models (1B-7B) with optimized kernels.
[09:00] Priya: About metrics: We need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency traces to show to execs.
[09:07] Jordan: Redwood Console includes token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and traces. We'll grant trial access during the pilot so you can see the metrics.
[09:18] Evan: Any gotchas with embedding dimensionality and downstream ranking quality?
[09:22] Samira: The main things: diminishing returns past certain dims for some corpora; also index efficiency and recall/precision tradeoffs. We recommend controlled A/Bs with your eval set. Redwood Optimize can give quantization and dimensionality recommendations.
[09:37] Alex: On the rerank front, do you do two-stage (bi-encoder candidate generation + cross-encoder rerank) in your hosted offering or do customers need Dedicated?
[09:45] Samira: Hosted can do two-stage but cross-encoder rerank cost/latency make Dedicated recommended for production at scale. You can pilot hosted rerank for functional verification.
[09:58] Priya: How are requests billed in Hosted — per embedding call + per rerank token?
[10:04] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based: per-embedding unit and per-token generation/rerank. Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing plus optional usage add-ons. We'll send the pricing summary.
[10:15] Marcus: For benchmarking, what sample size do you need? We can provide 500k vectors and a 10k query set.
[10:22] Samira: That's perfect. For meaningful numbers, a 10k query eval and a 500k-1M vector corpus is standard. We'll include a runbook with scripts to format and push vectors, run queries, and capture latency/throughput and quality metrics (MRR/NDCG).
[10:40] Evan: Can you outline the pilot timeline? We're hoping to move to a pilot in the next 2 weeks and a production decision in 6-8 weeks.
[10:50] Jordan: Typical pilot: 1) Kick-off + env setup (1 week), 2) benchmark runs + tuning (1 week), 3) analysis + follow-up (1 week). So 2-3 weeks is doable for pilot results. Production decision timing sounds reasonable.
[11:05] Priya: Any pre-reqs on our side?
[11:07] Samira: We'll need sample data, creds for your Pinecone if you want Redwood to integrate directly, and network details if you want Private. Also, expected QPS pattern.
[11:18] Evan: One more — can Redwood host a rerank model (weighing latency) but keep vectors in our Pinecone for control?
[11:25] Jordan: Yes — we've seen that hybrid. You can host rerank on Dedicated while vectors remain in Pinecone; the extra network hop can add latency but it's workable for many customers. If latency becomes an issue, moving vectors into Dedicated reduces that hop.
[11:40] Marcus: About monitoring and alerts — we need traceability for model regressions.
[11:46] Samira: Redwood Optimize and Console include quality monitoring tied to eval prompt sets, regression alerts, and rollback tooling for model rollouts. We'll attach examples.
[12:00] Alex: Any contractual minimums for Dedicated?
[12:05] Jordan: Dedicated typically involves reserved monthly capacity and a minimum term (depends on sizing). We'll include options in the pricing sheet — monthly and annual with discounts.
[12:18] Priya: For PII controls, can we restrict where embeddings are stored by tag?
[12:23] Samira: Yes, you can set data residency and bucket hot vs cold vectors, and on Private we can ensure embeddings never leave your VPC. We'll provide a whitepaper.
[12:35] Evan: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[12:38] Jordan: Recap: we'll send pricing/security docs and benchmarking runbook. You'll share sample dataset and query logs. We'll schedule a kick-off for the pilot next week. Any other asks?
[12:50] Priya: Maybe include a sample config for ef/search settings and recommended index parameters for 768 vs 1024.
[12:57] Samira: Will do.
[13:02] Evan: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[13:05] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
